newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil slips on crude falls.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil slips on crude falls.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were down at midday on Tuesday in quiet trade after falls to overnight crude prices amid weak fundamentals, traders said.
"Gas oil is reacting to crude, it went up yesterday because of crude and today its down because of crude," said a trader.
"The fundamentals have not changed. This market is still weak because of the prompt overhang."
August swaps were indicated at $21.05/$21.15 per barrel, down from Monday's $21.35/$21.45.
But July was down only slightly relative to August due to some short covering of the prompt month. July was last quoted at $20.50/$20.60, compared to Monday's $20.55/$20.65, brokers said.
As a result the contango narrowed further to value at about minus 50 cents compared to Monday's traded level of minus 75 cents and Friday's value of minus $1.00.
Overnight August Brent crude closed down 27 cents to $17.82 per barrel, virtually wiping out the gains from Monday and Friday.
Traders said they expect gas oil to trek at the lower level due to the surplus prompt cargoes.
Fuel oil swaps are steady with August and September last quoted unchanged at $98.00/$98.75.
